summary: Revise at 5.8 (Caiman 7, ship bar 7.5; for scale, Corvus was cut at 6.6). Two gates are missing from the JSON and one fails, so revise is automatic. report.json does not record the ray release at 0.100 or 0.075 mm or any draft-clamp bite. The template gate fails: template_gate_passed is false at 3,468,573 of 3,000,000 bytes, and it was run on the 27 Sep design, not on the round-1 design (its triangle count is 1,555,580, the export's is 1,580,130). Every recorded geometry gate is green. Artistically the round-1 ring is a crawling lizard figure on a polished half-round dome. In side.png and at full size it reads as 'a lizard'. At 300 px it does not read as a Gila monster. In face-300 the figure is a knobbly strip with a round bulb for a head and two pin-ball eyes standing on top like a frog's. The trunk and tail carry no black-and-salmon banding. The tail's rear half drops out of sight down the shoulder. The theme is split in three: a figure on top, a bald polished field across the face and shoulders, and a banded bead hide that starts at hard straight theta cut-offs and covers only the shank. The shank hide is the best passage. It has big and small bead fields in diagonal bands. But the band edges are stair-stepped like a raster mask, and hairline radial seams cut the beadwork at tile joins (palm.png centre, reverse.png top, side.png at about 5 and 7 o'clock). The spessartite sits in a plain collet on the bald field with nothing tying it to the animal. A concrete round can fix all of this, and two rounds remain.
strengths: It is the only Cataphracta ring built around a full-round figure. The silhouette in side.png (a lizard draped over the crown, legs gripping the shoulders) is unlike every Reptilia tile and every Cataphracta concept.

The figure is sculpted, not CAD. The limbs taper, the feet splay with separate toes, the jaw line is open in profile (side.png), and the hide on the body is irregular osteoderm pebbling, not a uniform grid.

The shank hide finally shows two bead sizes as bands (palm.png, reverse.png). Coarse pearl fields alternate with fine granulation in oblique bands that fork in places. This is the first round where banding reads at all.
The spessartite is in a made collet that stays visible from the face and in the hero, and its orange is the only colour on the ring.

Every geometry gate the JSON records is green at draft and at export. The export is 1,580,130 triangles and watertight, with 0 degenerate faces, 0 self-crossings on the ring, the figure and the pattern, 0 vertices in the bore, a Castable lost-wax verdict at the 0.8 mm section, 0 DFM findings, 1 stone reported and 1 previewed, and a cold reload that is identical.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Three separate treatments. The figure sits on the crown (theta about 40-140). A bald, mirror-polished field runs from the figure to the stone and across both shoulders (hero.png, face.png, shoulder.png). The banded bead hide starts at hard straight cut-offs across the band (the right edge of hero.png, the left of reverse.png) and covers only the shank. Nothing carries the animal's skin from the figure into the band.

checklist.item: The hide reads as this specific animal at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: hero-300 reads as 'a lizard crawling on a ring'. face-300 reads as a knobbly strip or caterpillar with frog-like pin eyes. There is no Gila banding on the figure, the head is not the broad flat Gila wedge, and the fat tail is lost down the shoulder. The shank bands read as granulation or 'urchin' work, not as Gila beadwork. A jeweller would say lizard or gecko, not Gila monster.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: The figure's outline is crisp. The hide bands are not: their edges step in pixel stairs across palm.png and reverse.png (raster mask edges), beads at band edges smear into teardrops, and hairline radial seams cross the beadwork at tile joins (palm.png on the centre line, reverse.png top centre, side.png at about 5 and 7 o'clock).

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: The spessartite is in a made collet (0.52 mm wall), clearly visible in hero, face and stones.png, with 1 reported and 1 previewed. It is weak as design: it floats on bald metal about 3 mm off the snout and relates to nothing.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: The figure is sculpted, but the band around it is an untouched polished half-round. The hide is switched on and off along straight theta lines, which reads as mechanical masking, not as skin wrapping a form.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Not applicable. The body is a procedural HalfRound profile with no factory stock. The edges are the intended rounded edges.

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Cataphracta rings and the Reptilia tiles
checklist.reason: The figure on the crown gives a silhouette no Reptilia tile or other Cataphracta concept has (side.png, contact-300).

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The large form (figure), medium forms (limbs, feet) and small forms (beads) exist, but about 40% of the visible face and shoulders is bald polish. Density is well below Caiman's fully worked hero, and the small forms are illegible at 300 px (face-300 is mush on the figure and blank off it).

gates.verified: geometry: watertight true, boundary 0, non-manifold 0, degenerate 0 at 768x320 (736,956 tris) and 1536x448 (1,580,130 tris).

gates.gate: 0 self-crossings on the ring and every made part
gates.verified: self_crossings 0; made.figure_self_crossings 0; pattern self_crossings 0; parts_notes []. The collet is joined (parts_joined 1).
vertices_inside 0 at draft and export. The closest vertex at 9.29986 mm against a 9.3 mm bore radius is f32 noise on the bore surface.
process LostWax, verdict Castable, thinnest wall 2.10 mm at theta 277. The two-part undercut (3.23%, worst -45.8 deg) is reported and not gated, as the process allows.

gates.gate: Ray release 0 obstructions and 0 unresolved at 0.100 and 0.075 mm
gates.verified: Not recorded anywhere in report.json. The earlier lost-wax-pattern read test 2 quoted a Blocked release (50 and 66 obstructions) on an older design. Unrecorded is an automatic revise.

gates.gate: Every draft-clamp bite at most 0.05 mm
gates.verified: No bite or clamp record in report.json for the eight 'Gila beadwork' layers. Earlier read tests quoted bites of 0.24 and 0.19 mm. Unrecorded is an automatic revise.

gates.gate: Template gate: at most 4 design.set patches within the class budget
gates.verified: template-verification.json and target/tpl/heloderma/verification.json: template_gate_passed false, class 'painted', 3,468,573 bytes against a 3,000,000 budget (size_review_required true). The patch count (1, /manufacturing) is fine. The run is stale: it is dated 27 Sep 20:10 and reports 1,555,580 triangles, while the round-1 export (design.ring.json dated 28 Sep 13:34) has 1,580,130.

gates.gate: Land widths (author's own gate: 'at the floor or named')
gates.verified: The gate passes only by naming: the Gila figure's thinnest_section is 0.00025 mm with 64.6 mm² under the 0.8 mm floor, and the collet's is 0.178 mm with 26.2 mm² under. The treatment admits 'a per-feature section check was not built'. Claw tips in reverse.png and shoulder.png are needle-thin. Not a review.md gate; flagged as a casting risk.

punch_list.change: Run mf::inspect plus mf::release::analyze on the lost-wax pattern at 0.100 and at 0.075 mm, and record obstructions and unresolved rays per resolution. Record the per-layer and composite draft-clamp bite (max mm and texels cut) for all eight 'Gila beadwork' layers, or record explicitly that no clamp is applied, with bite 0.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json has release.{0.100,0.075}.{obstructions:0, unresolved:0} and clamp.max_bite_mm <= 0.05 in both the draft and export blocks, each with a gate entry that passes.

punch_list.change: Re-run the template gate on the current design. Bring the painted template under 3,000,000 bytes: drop the eight hide atlases from 2048x768 toward 1536x576, merge the eight beadwork layers into one or two atlases, or move the bead lattice to procedural tiling with only the band mask painted.
punch_list.acceptance: template_gate_passed true, template_bytes <= 3,000,000, design_set_patches <= 4, and triangle count equal to the export's.

punch_list.zone: Face and shoulders, theta 20-160 outside the figure; hide cut-offs at about theta 20 and 160
punch_list.change: Stop leaving the face bald. Run the hide under and around the figure as a quiet ground of fine beads at most 0.10 mm high and pitch 0.6 mm or less. Keep a polished moat only 0.6-0.8 mm wide hugging the figure's outline and the collet. Replace the straight theta cut-offs with a feathered grade over at least 4 mm of arc into the banded shank hide.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero.png, face.png and shoulder.png no straight line across the band ends the hide, and no bare patch wider than 1 mm remains outside the moat. In hero-300 the figure still stands out as the brightest closed shape.

punch_list.zone: Figure: head, eyes and tail (the Gila mesh, theta about 40-140)
punch_list.change: Make it a Gila, not a generic lizard. Flatten and broaden the head into a blunt wedge as wide as the neck, with a 0.3 mm neck crease. Sink the pin-ball eyes into sockets on the head's sides with lids, with the eye at most 0.25 mm proud of the lid rather than standing on the crown. Bring the whole tail onto the face as a fat sausage whose base is at least 75% of trunk width, lying along the crest toward theta 140, not dropping down the shoulder.
punch_list.acceptance: In face-300 a head with a square snout can be pointed to at the stone end, the eyes no longer read as two balls above the outline, and the tail's full length and rounded tip are visible.

punch_list.zone: Figure dorsal surface, nape to tail tip
punch_list.change: Put the Gila banding on the animal itself. Make 4 dark bands on the trunk and 4-5 rings on the tail, each 1.5-2.0 mm wide with forked edges. Sink each dark band 0.25-0.30 mm below the pale-band envelope and fill it with fine beads 0.4-0.5 mm across. Pale bands get domed beads 0.9-1.1 mm across.
punch_list.acceptance: In face-300, 3-4 light/dark stripes can be counted on the trunk and 4 on the tail.

punch_list.zone: Shank hide (theta about 160-20 through 270), all eight Gila beadwork layers
punch_list.change: Remove the stair-stepped band borders: author the band mask as smooth SVG paths, or raise the mask resolution so that no step exceeds 0.05 mm. Close the hairline radial seams at the tile and layer joins by making the tiling period divide the circumference exactly and overlapping adjacent layers by at least one bead pitch.
punch_list.acceptance: At full size in palm.png, reverse.png and side.png, band edges read as curves with no pixel staircase, and no continuous line crosses the band at any theta.

punch_list.zone: Spessartite collet, theta 90 on the crest
punch_list.change: Tie the stone to the animal: move the snout to within 1 mm of the collet, or put the stone into a dorsal row of domes 0.42 mm high running away from it along crest_v. Give the collet a beaded (milgrain) lip so it belongs to the beadwork.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero-300 and face-300 the stone reads as part of the composition (at the snout or in a bead line), not as a separate dot on bare metal.

punch_list.zone: Figure claws, toe tips and eye moats
punch_list.change: Thicken claw and toe tips to at least 0.5 mm with rounded ends, and build the per-feature section check the land_widths note says is missing.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json Gila part: load-bearing features measured at 0.8 mm or more, with only named bead chords under the floor. No needle tips in reverse.png or shoulder.png.
